name: Grand Hotel Villa Serbelloni
positioning: Family-owned neoclassical villa hotel in Bellagio, at the tip of the promontory where Lake Como forks, with period interiors, gardens, a lakeside pool and a spa
best_for: Travelers who want a historic villa with period interiors on Lake Como
Couples who want lake swimming, gardens and a lakeside pool
Families who want an indoor kids pool, watersports and babysitting

facts.text: The hotel sits at the tip of the promontory where Lake Como forks, with views of the water and the mountains.
The hotel is a neoclassical villa.
The villa was built in 1854 as the lakeside estate of a countess and her family, and was converted into a hotel 20 years later.
Swiss businessman Arturo Bucher acquired the hotel in 1918, and the Bucher family has owned it for four generations.
Past guests include JFK and Winston Churchill.
The rooms are all different, each with its own 150-year history and period furnishings.
Bathrooms are marble-clad, with separate spaces for bath, toilet and shower.
The hotel has a palm-fringed lakeside pool.
The Luce del Lago Spa is a full-service spa next to an indoor pool with a water slide and jets.
A sandy beach area has a path down to the lake, and guests can swim out to a floating dock with a diving board.
The hotel has two restaurants, Mistral and La Goletta, led by chef Ettore Bocchia, a molecular gastronomist.
Live grand piano music plays in the villa every evening.

highlights.text: Silk leg-warmers on the beds are a Serbelloni trademark, replicas of 18th-century Como aristocracy bedcovers sewn by local seamstresses.
The interiors feature grand marble staircases, giant crystal chandeliers, Louis XVI and Art Nouveau furniture, and frescoed ceilings.
The Italianate garden has lush tropical plants and geometric hedges.
Guests can book the JFK or Churchill suites.
The hotel has a Riva boat guests can book.

considerations.text: The hotel is seasonal, open from April to November.
The lake bed is rocky, so water shoes are advised for lake swimming.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing and a formal atmosphere that may not suit casual travelers.
